content:
- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows recent downward momentum; reduce forecast by 5–10% in such contexts.  
- Underestimate prices after strong upward spikes (especially >70) if sentiment turns negative; add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion.  
- Forecast tends to lag true price drops by 2–4 days; adjust downward by 1–3% for each lagged day if sentiment is bearish.  
- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.37), forecast often overshoots; cap 30d forecast at +5% above recent 18-day average.  
- Mean reversion is stronger in 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% downward correction if true outcome deviates >5% from 18-day moving average.
